skill.name: doc-scanner
skill.description: Scans project documentation files for AI assistant guidance, summarizes conventions, and can help consolidate multiple assistant docs into one AGENTS.md.
skill.summary: Finds and summarizes project AI documentation for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Static matches for shell execution, environment variables, and reconnaissance are false positives: the cited lines are Markdown templates, inline examples, or ordinary headings, not executable code. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files. The main residual concern is overbroad Bash permission in SKILL.md for a documentation scanner that primarily needs file search, read, and controlled write access.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools unless a documented, bounded shell workflow is required. Prefer Glob and Read for scanning.

remediation.issue: Consolidation can write or archive guidance files
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating .doc-archive/ or writing a new AGENTS.md. Show proposed content first.
Keep environment variable examples generic and state that secrets must not be copied into generated documentation.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md grants Bash in allowed-tools, but the documented workflow describes Glob, Read, and Write operations for scanning and consolidation. Shell access increases the impact of prompt injection in project documentation and is not justified by the stated workflow.

content.value_statement: Project guidance is often split across AI, IDE, and terminal documentation files. This skill finds those files, summarizes their guidance, and helps create a unified AGENTS.md when appropriate.
actual_capabilities: Searches common guidance filenames such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, COPILOT.md, CURSOR.md, and WARP.md.
Reads discovered guidance files and identifies agent recommendations, workflows, conventions, and commands.
Prioritizes platform-neutral guidance before tool-specific documentation.
Summarizes multiple guidance sources into one project documentation overview.
Offers to create a consolidated AGENTS.md and archive originals when several guidance files exist.
Can generate a starter AGENTS.md from project structure and observed conventions when no guidance exists.
limitations: It depends on the assistant to read files safely and follow workspace permissions.
Generated AGENTS.md content should be reviewed before replacing existing guidance.
It focuses on documentation guidance, not full repository health or security auditing.
It may miss guidance stored in unusual filenames or non-Markdown sources.

use_cases.title: Onboard to an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Find existing AI and IDE guidance before making changes.

use_cases.title: Consolidate assistant instructions
use_cases.description: Merge scattered CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, WARP.md, and similar files into one clearer AGENTS.md.

use_cases.title: Prepare agent context
use_cases.description: Summarize workflows, conventions, and common commands before planning implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Find project guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this repository for AI assistant documentation. Summarize the files found, their priority, and the most important guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the discovered project documentation and summarize coding conventions, workflows, and commands that should guide my next task.

prompt_templates.title: Compare documentation sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare all assistant guidance files in this project. Identify overlapping instructions, conflicts, missing topics, and tool-specific notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a consolidated AGENTS.md
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the existing AI documentation and draft a unified AGENTS.md. Preserve source intent, flag conflicts, and ask before archiving or replacing files.

output_examples.input: A repository has AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and WARP.md.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the source list, highlights AGENTS.md as primary, separates Claude-specific notes, and recommends consolidation steps.

output_examples.input: No assistant documentation exists in a small Node project.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a starter AGENTS.md outline based on structure, package scripts, test folders, and visible conventions.

output_examples.input: Several guidance files disagree about test commands.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the conflict, cites the source files, and asks which command should become canonical.

best_practices: Review every generated or consolidated guidance file before writing it.
Keep AGENTS.md concise and link to deeper docs for long procedures.
Archive originals only after confirming the consolidated version preserves their intent.
anti_patterns: Do not replace existing guidance without showing the proposed changes first.
Do not treat tool-specific instructions as platform-neutral rules without context.
Do not copy secrets, tokens, or private environment values into generated documentation.

faq.question: Which files does it look for?
faq.answer: It targets AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, COPILOT.md, CURSOR.md, WARP.md, and related AI guidance files.

faq.question: Can it write files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can offer to create AGENTS.md and archive originals, but changes should be confirmed first.

faq.question: Does it run project commands?
faq.answer: Its documented workflow uses file search and reading. Command examples in templates are meant for documentation, not automatic execution.

faq.question: How does it handle conflicting instructions?
faq.answer: It should surface conflicts, keep source-specific notes, and ask before choosing one rule as canonical.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to find shared and tool-specific guidance for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other assistants.

faq.question: Does it audit repository security?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize assistant documentation. Use a dedicated security audit for vulnerability review.
